rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Top-of-file 'What you do:' line: 'Before you ship, ask the skill to disclose its own weakest part.' Neither fenced prompt enacts this. curriculum/prompts/author-test-strategy-skill-1.md ends 'When you have enough, write `~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md` as a personal skill (frontmatter with `name` + `description`, then instructions). Show me before saving.' — no self-critique ask. curriculum/prompts/author-test-strategy-skill-2.md asks Claude to grade the PRODUCED TEST STRATEGY ('is it good? Does it reflect how testing actually works on this codebase, or does it read generic?'), a different target than the SKILL.md file naming its own weakest part. This file's own maintainer 'Push-back moves' list (P1 question-dump / P1 generic answers / P1 missed detail / P2 invoke-skip / P2 invoke-output-weak / P3 ship-confusion) has no entry recovering this gap either. Re-verified against git history this pass: commit 677a584 (2026-04-28, 'AE101 M2: second exercise + mini-lecture + mechanical-tested') deleted an entire 'Phase 2: self-critique before shipping' beat — its own dedicated prompt reading 'Before I ship the test-strategy skill, I want you to critique it... Don't just reassure me. Name weak parts.' — while leaving the top-of-file promise verbatim. The parent module file (curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/earn-the-trust.md) still carries the beat as live in four places, confirmed by direct grep this pass: Key Concepts line 46 ('Ask the agent what's weakest about its own output; the mirror reflects what your own read would miss'), What You'll Learn line 24 ('Test the authored skill: ask it to disclose its own weakest part, push back on the critique...'), the failure-mode table line 122/166 ('Ex3 default-acceptance on first SKILL.md... Trainer runs the self-critique move'), and the compression guidance line 135 ('Compress Ex3's conversation phase, not the invocation-and-self-critique'). The strategy doc's M3-in-detail section names the same move as load-bearing: 'Force-push-back move: ask the skill to disclose its own weakest part before shipping... this IS theme #4 (mechanically self-aware) used as designed.' Four independent surfaces (this file's own top line, the module file ×4, the strategy doc, and the maintainer block's own 'Watch for: default-acceptance failure' note) still expect a beat this exercise file no longer contains a mechanism for.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either restore a self-critique ask inside a prompt fence (end of Phase 1, or a short reinstated Phase between authoring and invocation) or cut the top-of-file promise plus the module file's four matching references so body and mechanism agree again. Maintainer-approval-gated (check_prompts.md §22) if the fix touches a prompt fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: author-test-strategy-skill-1's last line: 'When you have enough, write `~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md`... Show me before saving.' Read literally, 'show me before saving' gates the persisted write behind an unscripted approval turn, while Phase 3's body asserts unconditionally: 'The skill is already shipped. It sits at ~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md. The agent wrote it there in Phase 1.' Low-severity in practice — a real conversation naturally continues with 'looks good, save it' (matches the sim trace's Phase 1 persona_action) — but the fence's own last imperative technically defers the load-bearing artifact past what the body assumes already happened.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If Phase 3's 'already shipped' framing must hold exactly, make the continuation explicit in the fence ('show me before saving; once I confirm, save it') rather than relying on inferred conversational flow.
